intro: Calendar questions ask which day of the week a date falls on, or how many days lie between dates. The key idea is odd days: the days left over after whole weeks.

tips.title: Odd days
tips.body: Divide the number of days by 7. The whole weeks change nothing; the remainder (the odd days) moves the weekday on. 100 days = 14 weeks + 2, so it's 2 days later.

tips.title: Number the weekdays
tips.body: Count 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, 2 = Tuesday … 6 = Saturday. Then "5 odd days from the start" means Friday.

tips.title: Month odd days
tips.body: A 31-day month has 3 odd days, a 30-day month 2, and February 0 (or 1 in a leap year).

tips.title: Year odd days
tips.body: An ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year 2. 100 years have 5, 200 years 3, 300 years 1 and 400 years 0.

tips.title: Leap years
tips.body: A year is a leap year if it divides by 4, but a century year (like 1900) only if it divides by 400. So 2000 was a leap year and 1900 wasn't.

tips.title: Counting days between dates
tips.body: Read the question carefully: "from 26 January to 15 May" in this book counts both days. Write each month's days and add them.
